caseStudies.title: Recognizing Arabic handwriting with deep learning
caseStudies.projectTitle: NAMAQ - Arabic Handwriting Recognition Using Deep Learning
caseStudies.summary: A character-recognition study addressing the variation and complexity of Arabic handwriting.
caseStudies.problem: Arabic handwritten characters vary in shape and writing style, making automated recognition a challenging classification problem.
approach: Use convolutional neural networks to extract handwriting features.
Apply machine-learning classifiers to distinguish Arabic character classes.
Evaluate the recognition approach using the handwriting datasets described in the project record.
caseStudies.contribution: The project record lists me as Co-Investigator, alongside Wareef Yousuf Aljomaee and Saeed M Alshahrani. The recorded work focuses on CNN feature extraction and Arabic character classification.
caseStudies.outcome: The CV project record reports a 96.4% recognition rate across 29 Arabic character classes.
caseStudies.evidenceNote: This figure is a reported project result, not a guarantee of performance on other datasets, writing styles, or real-world deployments. The website does not provide a reproducible benchmark package or a full error analysis.
caseStudies.nextQuestion: How well would the approach generalize to handwriting collected from different writers and settings?

caseStudies.title: Making health information accessible through an iOS advisory application
caseStudies.projectTitle: COVID-19 Advising Application for Apple Devices (iOS)
caseStudies.summary: An NLP-based mobile application explored in the context of COVID-19 health information and symptom-related guidance.
caseStudies.problem: People seeking COVID-19 information need accessible digital interfaces that can interpret their questions and present relevant guidance.
approach: Develop an iOS application focused on health-related advisory interactions.
Use natural-language processing for symptom-related input.
Consider the security and safety characteristics of the mobile platform as part of the application design.
caseStudies.contribution: The project record lists me as Principal Investigator. It describes the development of an NLP-based iOS advisory application and links to the associated research publication.
caseStudies.outcome: The documented output is a mobile healthcare advisory application and a supporting publication in PeerJ Computer Science.
caseStudies.evidenceNote: The website record does not establish clinical validation, diagnostic accuracy, comparative patient outcomes, or current availability of the application. This is presented as computing research, not a replacement for medical care.
caseStudies.nextQuestion: How can advisory interfaces communicate uncertainty and be evaluated with appropriate healthcare-domain expertise?

caseStudies.title: Building digital trust into academic credential verification
caseStudies.projectTitle: Blockchain-Based Digitally Secured Model for Educational Sector
caseStudies.summary: A blockchain-based model for academic certificate verification in the Saudi education context.
caseStudies.problem: Verifying academic documents requires trustworthy records and a way to address document fraud without making verification unnecessarily difficult.
approach: Apply blockchain and cryptographic mechanisms to certificate verification.
Design a digitally secured verification model for the education sector.
Study how transparent verification can support digital transformation in academic administration.
caseStudies.contribution: The project record lists me as Principal Investigator. The recorded contribution is the development of a blockchain-based academic certificate verification system and model.
caseStudies.outcome: The documented output is a credential-verification model with a supporting PeerJ Computer Science publication.
caseStudies.evidenceNote: The website does not provide transaction throughput, operating cost, independent security audit results, or institution-wide deployment measurements. Claims about scale and effectiveness should be assessed against the supporting publication.
caseStudies.nextQuestion: Which parts of this verification approach could inform accountable data provenance in other sectors, including healthcare?
